stem:
Aarav walks from his home to the bus stop, waits there, and then walks on to school. He covers 240 m in 120 s, stands still at the bus stop for 60 s, and then covers another 360 m in 120 s.

What is Aarav's average speed for the whole journey from home to school?

options.text: 2 m/s, because he walked 240 m in 120 s in the first part
2 m/s, because the total distance of 600 m is divided by the total time of 300 s
3 m/s, because 360 m divided by 120 s gives his fastest walking speed
2.5 m/s, because the total distance of 600 m is divided by only the walking time of 240 s

teacher.key_rationale: Average speed = total distance / total time = (240 + 360) m / (120 + 60 + 120) s = 600/300 = 2 m/s. Option A uses only the first segment, C uses only the fastest segment, and D wrongly excludes the waiting time from the total time; all are non-uniform-motion traps. B correctly includes the stationary interval.
